To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mixed layer response to Hurricane Lini was weaker than expected and was likely due to a combination of the storm’s relatively weak intensity and the Loop Current’s position in a region of weak vertical stratification.
the Loop Current mixed layer response to Hurricane Lilli was weaker than previously reported.
the Loop Current mixed layer temperature cooled <1°C and the vertical current shear associated mixed layer currents was up to 50 percent weaker, on average.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ocean response to Hurricane Lilli.
the impact of tropical cyclones (TCs) on the Gulf of Mexico (GOM) Loop Current and its adjacent waters.
the oceanic response to Hurricane Lilli’s passage over the Gulf of Mexico and the Loop Current.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Hurricane Lili did indeed cause a cooling of the Loop Current, but not to the degree that was previously observed.
the Loop Current and mixed layer energy response to Hurricane Lilli was significantly less than that observed in previous studies of other storms.
Hurricane Lili’s passage over the Loop Current resulted in a mixed layer cooling of <1°C and a decrease in Loop Current velocity of 0.18 ±.25 m s− 1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Loop Current mixed layer energy response to Hurricane Lilli (2002) was weak, and that this was due to the Loop Current’s position relative to the storm.
the Loop Current was not significantly impacted by the hurricane and that the mixed layer response to the storm was not typical of previous hurricanes that have passed through the region.
the Loop Current mixed layer energy response to Hurricane Lilli (2002) was significantly less than expected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mixed layer energy response to Hurricane Lini is much weaker than previously reported for hurricanes that have impacted the Loop Current in the same general area.
the Loop Current mixed layer response to Hurricane Lilia (2002) is not as strong as previous studies have shown.
the Loop Current is not as sensitive to tropical cyclone forcing as previously thought.
